opening_message:
Ticket 1: Mary Lee (employee ID E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E015.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. Per policy, full-time employees can have up to write access (admin only if their role owns the system); Analyst does not own Source Code, so the maximum is write. Recommended: write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E015 is a contractor with basic security training (note: differs from earlier note listing full-time). Contractors max is read without advanced training; request for admin exceeds maximum, so grant max = read.
reason: Mary Lee (E015) requested admin access to Source Code. HR (the authoritative source on employment status) lists her as a full-time Analyst. Per policy, full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system; Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Analyst, so the maximum allowed is write. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, so the maximum is granted: write. (Note: the Security agent's conflicting contractor classification is not used for employment status, and its recommended level of read is lower than the permissible maximum from HR's record.)

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Mary Lee (E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

There are conflicting notes:
- HR agent says: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation: write. Per policy, full-time employees can have up to write; Analyst doesn't own Source Code, so max is write. Requested admin. Grant max = write.
- Security agent says: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read. Contractors max is read without advanced training. Requested admin. Grant max = read.

The two notes conflict on employment type. HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Who to trust? Hmm. The HR agent note is about employment facts (HR knows employment type). Security agent notes the difference. Typically HR is authoritative for employment type. The policy is based on employment type. HR says full-time, so max = write (since Analyst doesn't own Source Code). Requested admin > write, so grant write.

But wait - Security says contractor. There's a conflict. Which note do we use? The Approver needs to make a final decision. Let me think about the evidence. HR agent is the one who writes employee facts about employment. Security's database may be outdated or it may be correct. HR's note seems more authoritative for employment type.

The recommendation: HR recommends write; Security recommends read. Given the conflicting info, the decision should be based on the most reliable source. HR determines employment type. So full_time, max write, grant write since requested admin exceeds max.

Actually, let me carefully consider. The policy: full_time employees up to write, admin only if role owns the system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns Source Code). So max = write. Requested admin > max, grant max = write.

I'll submit write with reasoning citing HR's note as authoritative on employment status, and policy.

Let me submit decision.
